subject: Clarification on region pin scope, transient copies, and deletion evidence
messages:
From: Lisa Murray <lisa.murray@finsecure.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finsecure.com
Date: 2026-05-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on pinning behavior and hidden copies

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a couple of follow-ups specific to the Dedicated cluster you described (we're planning to pin a production tenant to a US-dedicated pool):

1) When a tenant is "region-pinned" to a Redwood Dedicated pool, can you confirm whether any automatic snapshots, backups, or async replicas are ever stored outside the pinned region/availability zone? We need a clear list of potential transient copies and where they live.

2) If we request deletion of that tenant (data erasure), what artifacts remain (snapshots, logs, monitoring indices) and how long before each artifact is purged? Practical timeline and proof-of-deletion artifacts are ideal.

3) Are there any cross-region telemetry or diagnostic uploads (to Redwoods central control plane) that include tenant-level data? If so, what retention and masking controls apply?

Can you point us to any runbooks or sample evidence you can share? Appreciate a short, itemized response we can use in our compliance pack.

Regards,
Lisa Murray
Head of Security Programs
FinSecure

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Murray <lisa.murray@finsecure.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-15T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on pinning behavior and hidden copies

Hi Lisa — thanks, great questions. Short answers up front, then specifics and attachments (scrub playbook + snapshot diagram).

Summary (high level):
- Region pinning binds active tenant traffic, model serving, and persistent storage to the selected region (e.g., us-west-2).
- Transient copies: short-lived in-region snapshots and KV-cache checkpoints are created for operational reasons; asynchronous replication to another region is NOT enabled by default for Dedicated pinned pools. Cross-region copies only exist when explicitly configured (e.g., for DR) and require a written customer agreement.
- Deletion: we run a multi-step erasure: live data delete -> index/snapshot sweep -> secure wipe of ephemeral caches -> metadata tombstone. Proof artifacts include audit logs, snapshot deletion records, and a signed erasure attestation. Typical timeline: 0-72 hours for live data removal, 7-30 days for snapshot/index purge depending on retention policies and backup windows.

Details:
1) Snapshots and backups
- Automatic snapshots: created for point-in-time recovery inside the same region. They are retained per your backup policy (default 30 days but configurable). Snapshots are stored in the region where the dedicated storage volume is attached.
- Backups to object storage are region-scoped unless you enable cross-region replication.

2) Asynchronous replicas and DR
- For Dedicated we do not enable cross-region async replication by default. If a customer needs geo-redundancy, that's a specific configuration in the onboarding (and it's tracked as a contractual change).

3) Audit/telemetry uploads
- Health telemetry (metrics/aggregates) is sent to Redwood control-plane for platform health; it contains no raw tenant input data. When diagnostic bundles are requested (for an investigation), they are generated on-demand and redacted by default, but we can produce tenant-scoped bundles for compliance review under NDA.

Attachments: redwood-runtime-scrub-playbook.pdf (procedure + timelines), snapshot-diagram.png (illustration of where snapshots live).

If helpful I can add a technical note from Karthik with low-level details on snapshot lifecycle and block-level replication.

Best,
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, Lisa Murray <lisa.murray@finsecure.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-16T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on pinning behavior and hidden copies

Hi Lisa / Monica — adding a few technical specifics to back Monica's summary.

Operational copies we create (and where they live):
- Volume snapshots: created in-region and backed by the same region's object store. Snapshot metadata references the region and AZ.
- KV-cache checkpoints: in-memory and flushed to ephemeral disks in the same host cluster; these disks are ephemeral and wiped on host drain. No off-host copy is made unless a support bundle is requested.
- Support/diagnostic bundles: stored in the control plane for a configurable TTL (default 14 days), encrypted at rest; bundles are redacted and do not include full raw prompts unless explicitly requested.

Deletion mechanics and evidence:
- Step 1: Soft delete tenant record (0-2 hours) so no new reads/writes are possible.
- Step 2: Live data purge (0-72 hours): delete objects, record deletions in the audit log.
- Step 3: Snapshot sweep: remove snapshot references and schedule blob cleanup. Blob disposal is subject to underlying object-store garbage collection; typical completion 7-30 days.
- Step 4: Ephemeral host scrub on next maintenance window (within 7 days) and metadata tombstone.

Evidence we provide on request:
- Audit log slices (timestamped entries showing deletion API calls).
- Snapshot deletion manifest (listing snapshot ids and deletion timestamps).
- Host scrub confirmation notes (operator-run logs).
- Signed attestation statement summarizing timeline and artifacts.

Notes and caveats:
- If you have cross-region DR enabled, those replica artifacts will also need to be scrubbed per the same workflow; that is a customer-configured option and is surfaced in onboarding paperwork.
- For legal holds or eDiscovery we provide a hold workflow that pauses purge and provides a manifest of impacted artifacts.

Happy to run a short technical call if you want to walk through exact API calls and a sample artifact set.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

To: Lisa Murray <lisa.murray@finsecure.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on pinning behavior and hidden copies

Lisa — thanks for raising these. A couple of practical next steps from our side so your audit packet is complete: 

- We will produce a sample deletion evidence bundle (audit slice + snapshot deletion manifest + signed attestation). Expect the bundle in 3 business days.
- If you want granular object ids for the tenant's snapshots, we can include that; will require a short verification step from your side (security contact verification).
- If FinSecure plans to enable cross-region DR later, let's schedule a run-through of the added retention/erase implications.

Let me know where to drop the evidence (we can share on the Drive link above or upload to your secure SFTP).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
